To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the XZP + d and XZP+1d basis sets provide an excellent description of the second-row elements, which is essential for obtaining accurate atomization energies and vibrational properties.
the XZP + d and XZP + d-DKH basis sets are suitable for high-accuracy calculations of ZPVEs and atomization energies of molecules containing second-row elements.

the XZP + d and XZP+1d-DKH (where DKH stands for Douglas–Kroll-Hess) basis sets are well suited to obtain accurate atomization energies for molecules containing second-row elements, with an accuracy of 0.2–0.5 kcal mol–1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of all-electron basis sets, including inner polarization functions, for the elements from B to Ar.
the application of the recently developed segmented all-electron double- and triple-zeta basis sets for the second row of the periodic table.
a new set of all-electron basis sets that are designed for accurate calculations of molecular properties at the coupled cluster level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the XZP + 1d basis sets provide a reliable and cost-effective tool for high-quality molecular calculations.

the new basis sets, in conjunction with the CCSD(T) level of theory, are suitable to obtain reliable atomization energies for molecules containing the elements H, C, N, O, F, Ne, Na, Mg, Al, Si, P, S, Cl, and Ar.
the new basis sets are able to predict the ZPVEs and atomization energies of second-row compounds with an accuracy of 0.5–0.6 % and 0.8–1.0 %, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the XZP +1d-DKH and XZP+1d-DKH sets, in conjunction with the Douglas–Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian, provide a reliable description of the molecular properties of molecules containing elements from H to Kr, with the exception of the first-row elements, for which the XZP-DKH and XZD-DKH sets are preferred.
the XZP +1d and X2P +1d-DKH (X2 = D, T) basis sets are well suited for the study of the electronic and vibrational properties of second-row molecules.
for all of the molecules considered here, the errors in the ZPVEs were smaller than 0,5 %, and the atomization energies were improved by up to 2 kcal  mol−1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of tight d “inner polarization” functions in conjunction with XZP basis sets is a very effective approach for obtaining accurate molecular properties for molecules with second-row atoms.
for the second-row molecules, the inclusion of the tight d functions in the XZP basis set is essential for obtaining accurate atomization energies and ZPVEs.
the inclusion of tight inner d functions is crucial for obtaining accurate ZPVEs and atomization energies at the coupled cluster level.
